'''Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2lagsN0 Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed September 2017</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Mississippi and Alabama under the Gulf of Mexico to Florida.<ref name=source1/>

==Background==
The Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline is operated by Williams Partners L.P. It is jointly owned by Williams (50%) and Spectra Energy Partners L.P. (50%).<ref>[http://co.williams.com/operations-2/atlantic-gulf-operating-area/gulfstream/ Gulfstream], Williams, accessed January 2018</ref> It was the first and is still the largest gas pipeline in the Gulf of Mexico.<ref>[https://www.hydrocarbons-technology.com/projects/gulfstream-natural-gas-pipeline/ Gulfstream Natural Gas Pipeline], Hydrocarbons Technology, accessed January 2018</ref>

===Phase IV Expansion Project (Bartow Lateral)===


==Expansion projects==

=== Phase VI Expansion Project ===
According to the U.S.'s Energy Information Agency (EIA), the expansion will increase the operating pressure of the Gulfstream pipeline, to serve Tampa Electric Company's Big Bend power plant.<ref name=eia>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects] Energy Information Agency, accessed July 21, 2020</ref> The project is a part of a larger project aimed at converting the Big Bend Power Plant from coal to natural gas.<ref>Marlena Carollo, [https://www.tampabay.com/business/tampa-electric-is-cutting-down-coal-at-big-bend-but-is-natural-gas-the-right-alternative-20190308/ Tampa Electric is cutting down coal at Big Bend. But is natural gas the right alternative?], Tampa Bay Times, March 8, 2019</ref>

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project has applied for FERC approval, and as of October 2022 it was under construction.<ref name=eiaapr21>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php U.S. natural gas pipeline projects], U.S. Energy Information Administration, April 29, 2021</ref>
